title: Unscoped gateway endpoint-binding listing is admin-only; endpoint-scoped listing checks endpoint read
answers: can a normal user list all gateway endpoint bindings
who can see gateway endpoint bindings across endpoints
restrict endpoint binding listing to administrators
body:
Invariant: GET gateway/endpoints/bindings/list without endpoint_id is restricted to administrators; a non-admin gets 403.
With endpoint_id supplied, the check becomes the read permission on that specific gateway endpoint, so users with read on the endpoint can list its bindings.
Enforced by the bindings-list validator in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py, exercised by test_gateway_endpoints_permissions in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py.
Skipping this lets any authenticated user enumerate bindings for endpoints they have no access to.
applies: Authorization of gateway endpoint binding list routes; does not cover create or delete binding routes.
says: Non-admin users get permission denied when viewing all AI gateway endpoint bindings at once.
Restrict viewing global gateway endpoint bindings across the organization to workspace administrators.
Allow team members with read access to view bindings for their specific gateway endpoint.
Viewing endpoint bindings without choosing a specific gateway endpoint results in an authorization error.
Prevent standard users from enumerating gateway endpoint bindings for endpoints they cannot access.
search: Listing gateway endpoint bindings via GET gateway/endpoints/bindings/list requires administrator privileges when endpoint_id is omitted, returning 403 for non-admins. When endpoint_id is provided, the authorization check validates read permission for that specific gateway endpoint. This rule is enforced in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py and tested in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_gateway_endpoints_permissions, applying only to binding list routes and not create or delete binding routes.
